chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:
If her husband dies while absent from her, she observes the waiting period (iddah) from the time the news reaches her, because she intends to mourn for him.
ai.seo_question: When does a wife's waiting period begin if her husband dies while he is away?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies that the iddah for a widow whose husband dies in absence begins upon the arrival of news, not the actual death or return, as the intent is to facilitate her mourning period. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential focus on the practical commencement of legal obligations based on the wife's awareness, distinguishing it from other schools of thought that may emphasize the moment of death itself.
